images.caption: Figure 1:Audio-guided facial restoration from AIGC footage.Small facial regions provide limited evidence for lip and teeth structure. The model restores these regions using reference frames and accompanying audio. The three clips illustrate the source scenes and reconstructed heads; the reference bank depicts training-time conditioning. Quantitative references originate from the GT first frame. “Cat” denotes channel-wise fusion implemented by separate linear projections and summation.

Figure 2:Audio-guided facial video restoration.Stage 1 jointly trains on degraded images and videos with their corresponding targets. Images use only flow-matching MSE (ℒMSE\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MSE}}) and RGB losses; videos additionally use temporal supervision. Stage 2 uses degraded dubbed sources and target audio for lip correction. Sparse references and continuous history occupy distinct conditioning slots. The VAE, HuBERT, and SyncNet are frozen; the video DiT and conditioning projections are trainable. AIGC thumbnails illustrate the input and target roles.

Figure 3:Facial detail and articulation in AIGC scenes.Four MiniMax-H3[48]clips are shown with matched-time head crops located by orange boxes.Left:restoration under original audio.Right:FlashVSR Full (top) or SparkVSR (bottom) is followed by the arrow-marked dubbing methods; Input and SR-only outputs provide visual controls. Ours+jointly reconstructs detail and articulation with a GPT-Image-enhanced reference, without an external SR frontend. Waveforms and word-level IPA labels identify the audio segments. Displayed predictions are unretouched.

Figure 4:Qualitative ablation comparison.Each row shows two selected frames from one clip: MEAD[32](top) and HDTF[33](bottom). The same frame pair is displayed for GT and each model variant, with ten images per row. All variants use the GT first frame, and predictions are extracted directly from native RGB outputs.
